track_strategy: Recover only after Mark or Mike explicitly returns an unbooked request or quiet post-demo prospect to Marketing. The unbooked cycle removes scheduling friction without repeating the acquisition case. The post-demo cycle reopens one verified workflow, then closes respectfully. Each email has one action, replies route to the assigned sales owner, and quiet contacts move to Prospect Pulse only after the relevant recovery cycle ends. The client-retention claim appears once, in the workflow-led post-demo email, where it supports continuity rather than pressure.
open_questions: Who should appear as the named sender and signer for Marketing recovery emails?
Confirm the final [BOOKING URL] and whether it routes by assigned sales owner.
Which ActiveCampaign field records explicit Sales handback and the assigned sales owner for reply routing?
Should [WORKFLOW THEY CARED ABOUT] be populated manually from demo notes or through a controlled custom field?
Confirm the provisional handback intervals with Mark and Mike before activation.

strategy.what_why: A scheduling recovery note whose only job is to make the requested walkthrough easy to book without replaying the acquisition argument.
strategy.for_whom: Prospects who made a real request, then went quiet after personal Sales outreach; timing or format may be the blocker.
strategy.reach: Send from Marketing only after explicit handback, keep the note short, give one booking link, and route replies to the sales owner.
strategy.impact: Name the unfinished scheduling step plainly and give the prospect permission to suggest a different timing or format.

directions.name: One direct path
directions.summary: Acknowledge the request, provide the calendar path, and offer a reply for timing or format friction.
directions.draft:
Dear #Name#,

You asked to see LUCI, but we never found a time that worked. Rather than restart the conversation, here is one direct path to the walkthrough.

Pick a time: [BOOKING URL]

If timing or format is what held things up, reply here and tell us what would work better. Your reply will go to the sales owner who handled your request. We’ll take it from there.

directions.name: Name the friction
directions.summary: Normalize calendar or format friction and ask what kind of walkthrough would be more useful.
directions.draft:
Dear #Name#,

Sometimes the meeting request is still right, but the calendar or format is not. If that is what happened with your LUCI walkthrough, you can choose a different time here:

Choose a time: [BOOKING URL]

If a standard walkthrough is not the right format, reply with what would be more useful. The sales owner who handled your request will receive your note directly.

directions.name: Keep it simple
directions.summary: Lead with the booking link and assure the prospect that they will not need to repeat their original reason for reaching out.
directions.draft:
Dear #Name#,

We’ll keep this simple. The LUCI walkthrough you requested is still available, and this link is the quickest way to put it back on the calendar:

Schedule the walkthrough: [BOOKING URL]

If the timing has changed, reply here instead. Your note will go directly to the sales owner who handled your request, without asking you to repeat the reason you reached out.

emails.why_won: It acknowledges the request, identifies the incomplete step, and moves immediately to one scheduling action. The final also gives timing and format an easy reply path.

emails.primary_message: This scheduling sequence is ending, but the invitation remains open whenever a LUCI walkthrough becomes useful.

strategy.what_why: The respectful end of active scheduling, with one final booking path and an accurate transition to occasional notes.
strategy.for_whom: Prospects who requested a walkthrough but stayed quiet after personal Sales outreach and the first recovery email.
strategy.reach: Send from Marketing 7–10 days after the first recovery note, keep the link available, route replies to Sales, and end the active sequence.
strategy.impact: State the close plainly, say no action is needed, and preserve the invitation without a deadline.

directions.name: Close the sequence, not the door
directions.summary: End active scheduling while keeping the calendar and reply paths available.
directions.draft:
Dear #Name#,

We’re closing this scheduling sequence, but not the invitation. If a LUCI walkthrough still makes sense, you can choose a time here:

Schedule a walkthrough: [BOOKING URL]

If now is not the right time, no action is needed. We’ll keep you on the list for occasional notes, and you can return whenever the timing is better. A reply will go directly to the sales owner who handled your request.

directions.name: No action needed
directions.summary: Lead with permission to do nothing and explain that the invitation remains available.
directions.draft:
Dear #Name#,

If the timing for a LUCI walkthrough is not right, there is nothing you need to do. This is the last note in the active scheduling sequence.

The invitation stays open: [BOOKING URL]

We’ll send occasional notes from here, and you can reply whenever the conversation becomes useful again. Any reply will go directly to the sales owner who handled your request.

directions.name: Keep the link
directions.summary: Give the prospect the calendar link for later and distinguish occasional notes from continued booking requests.
directions.draft:
Dear #Name#,

Here is the scheduling link one last time so you have it if the timing changes:

Choose a time for the LUCI walkthrough: [BOOKING URL]

We won’t keep asking you to book. If you remain on our list, you’ll receive occasional notes instead. You can use the link or reply to this email whenever you want to pick the conversation back up.

emails.winner: Close the sequence, not the door
emails.why_won: The opening ends active scheduling while preserving the invitation. The final adds explicit permission to take no action and describes future contact without overpromising frequency.

emails.title: Relevant reason to reconsider

emails.sender: LUCI Marketing; replies route to the assigned sales owner
emails.audience: Net-new prospects explicitly handed back to Marketing after a demo and personal Sales follow-up
emails.primary_message: If the workflow discussed in the demo is still a priority, LUCI offers one operating path and a team that stays involved.

strategy.what_why: A post-demo recovery note built around one verified priority, giving the prospect a relevant reason to reconsider without retelling the demo.
strategy.for_whom: Prospects who completed a demo, received personal follow-up, and were explicitly handed back after going quiet.
strategy.reach: Send from Marketing 10–14 days after the final personal Sales attempt. Mark must populate the workflow from demo notes before activation, and replies return to the sales owner.
strategy.impact: Use one specific workflow, connect it to one-interface operation and the embedded team, and use the client-retention claim as continuity proof.

directions.name: Revisit the workflow
directions.summary: Open on the verified demo priority, connect it to one interface and the embedded team, then ask whether it remains active.
directions.draft:
Dear #Name#,

One point from your LUCI demo may still be worth revisiting: [WORKFLOW THEY CARED ABOUT].

LUCI can bring that work into one interface while the embedded team stays involved after the demo. That continuity matters: we've never lost a client.

If this priority is still active, reply with what has changed or what you still need to solve. Your reply will go directly to the sales owner who met with you.

directions.name: Is the priority still active?
directions.summary: Ask the status question first, then show how LUCI connects the workflow to the wider operating record.
directions.draft:
Dear #Name#,

Is [WORKFLOW THEY CARED ABOUT] still an active priority for your property?

If it is, LUCI can bring the screens, sources, controls, and operating record behind that workflow into one interface. The embedded team stays involved as the operation changes.

Reply with the part that still needs to work better. The sales owner who joined your demo will receive your note directly and continue from there.

directions.name: One reason to look again
directions.summary: Frame the demo workflow as part of the wider A/V operation instead of an isolated task.
directions.draft:
Dear #Name#,

There is one practical reason to look again at the workflow you raised in your demo: [WORKFLOW THEY CARED ABOUT] does not have to sit apart from the rest of the A/V operation.

LUCI brings that work into the same interface and keeps an embedded team alongside it.

If that problem is still worth solving, reply here. Your note will go directly to the sales owner who met with you.

emails.why_won: It starts with the prospect’s verified priority, makes one concise platform-and-partnership case, and asks a useful question without inventing personalization.

emails.cta_label: Reply if the priority is still active
emails.automation_notes: Send only after the final personal Sales attempt, explicit handback, and a verified demo note for the workflow placeholder. A reply, booking, or active opportunity stops all marketing automation and returns the contact to the assigned sales owner. Opens and ordinary clicks are reporting signals only. Do not activate while the placeholder is unpopulated. Timing remains provisional.
emails.guardrail_notes: Populate one verified workflow from demo notes; never infer it. Three approved hook options for Mark are: staging changes — prepare screens, sources, and audio behind the scenes, then apply the plan on cue; live screen verification — confirm what a TV or LED wall is playing without walking the floor; audit and access — see who changed what and when, then manage roles and sessions from the same operating view. Use one hook only. The body uses 'we've never lost a client' once as continuity proof, not pressure.

emails.title: Close the loop
emails.sender: LUCI Marketing; replies route to the assigned sales owner
emails.audience: Net-new prospects still quiet after post-demo recovery
emails.primary_message: The active follow-up is ending, and the prospect can resume the LUCI conversation whenever the timing becomes right.

strategy.what_why: The final post-demo recovery note, closing active follow-up while keeping reply and optional booking paths available.
strategy.for_whom: Prospects who completed a demo and personal follow-up, then stayed quiet after one relevant Marketing recovery email.
strategy.reach: Send from Marketing 7–10 days after the first post-demo recovery note. Make reply the human path and the booking link an optional convenience.
strategy.impact: Say the sequence is ending, avoid interpreting silence, and promise to pick up from the useful part of the prior conversation.

directions.name: Pick up where it matters
directions.summary: Close active follow-up, acknowledge changing priorities, and preserve reply and calendar paths.
directions.draft:
Dear #Name#,

We’re closing this follow-up sequence for now. Your priorities or timing may have changed, and there is no need to respond unless the conversation is still useful.

When the timing is right, reply here and we’ll pick up from the point that matters to you. You can also choose a time directly:

Restart the conversation: [BOOKING URL]

We’ll keep the door open and send only occasional notes in the meantime.

directions.name: No explanation needed
directions.summary: Remove any obligation to explain the silence and route a future reply back to the prior sales owner.
directions.draft:
Dear #Name#,

We haven’t heard back, so we’ll close this active follow-up without asking you to explain. Priorities move.

If the LUCI conversation becomes useful again, reply to this note and the sales owner who met with you will pick it up from there.

If you would rather choose a time directly, use [BOOKING URL]. Until then, you’ll hear from us only occasionally.

directions.name: Leave the next move with them
directions.summary: Make this the explicit final active note and leave control of the next step with the prospect.
directions.draft:
Dear #Name#,

This is the last note in our active follow-up after your LUCI demo.

We’ll leave the next move with you. Reply whenever the original priority becomes active again, or choose a time here: [BOOKING URL].

Your reply will go directly to the sales owner who met with you, so the conversation can continue from the useful part rather than beginning again. We’ll send only occasional notes in the meantime.

emails.why_won: It closes the sequence in the opening, allows for changed priorities without guessing, and offers reply before the optional calendar path.
